title: Keep secret literals out of source

facts.note: The detector scans source and template files, both existing and newly written content. Files ending in .example/.sample/.template and vendored/build directories are excluded.
Exclusions come from the source exceptions.

values: SECURITY-HARDCODED-SECRET-001: AWS access key id, PEM private-key header, or password/api-key/token assigned a string literal present in a covered file
facts.note: Content-level pattern finding emitted by bun_security_hygiene_detector, which reads assignment shape. It applies to any literal present in a covered file, not only newly added ones.

fires: A covered source or template file assigns a string literal to a variable or field named password, api key or token
A covered source or template file contains an AWS access key id, whether or not it is assigned to anything
A covered source or template file contains a PEM private-key header, whether or not it is assigned to anything
A secret literal was already in a covered file before the current change
doesNotFire: The credential is read from process.env at the edge
The literal sits in a .example, .sample or .template placeholder file
The file is in a vendored or build directory

A random-looking string that matches none of the patterns: it is not an AWS access key id, not a PEM private-key header, and not assigned to a password/api-key/token name. Entropy alone is not judged.

given: A source or template file that the secret scan covers
when: The file contains an AWS access key id, a PEM private-key header, or a password/api-key/token assigned a literal string, whether the literal is new or was already there
then: Source MUST NOT contain a secret literal.
prefer: Move the value to the environment and read it at the edge, e.g. `const apiKey = process.env.API_KEY;`
If the literal was ever committed, rotate the credential. Removing the line is not enough.
avoid: Writing a working credential inline, e.g. `const apiKey = "sk_live_0123456789abcdef";`, even temporarily to get unblocked
Treating deletion of a committed secret as the fix, because git keeps it
unless: The file is a `.example`, `.sample` or `.template` placeholder file. These are documentation, not secrets.
The file is in a vendored or build directory. These are never scanned.
The value is read from `process.env`. This is never a literal and is not matched.
why: Git keeps a committed secret, so deleting it does not fix it. Only rotating it does, which is why detection has to happen before the commit rather than in review.
evidence: bun_security_hygiene_detector reports no SECURITY-HARDCODED-SECRET-001 finding on any covered source or template file
Credentials in covered files are read from process.env
For any secret that was previously committed, the credential has been rotated (not just deleted)
verifier_detail: Scans source and templates for the five transcribed secret patterns. These cover AWS access key ids, PEM private-key headers, and password / api-key / token assigned a literal string.

Matching uses assignment shape, not entropy. This catches the realistic case (someone pasting a working key to get unblocked) and deliberately does not judge whether a random-looking string is secret.
Skip files ending in .example / .sample / .template. Never scan vendored or build directories. Do not match values read from process.env.
The patterns are language-neutral (`password = "..."` and a PEM header look identical in Python and TypeScript), so the Bun and python-pytest providers produce the same findings.
Term secret_literal: a credential written into source: an AWS key id, a PEM private-key header, or a password / api-key / token assigned a literal string.
Term rotation_not_deletion: the actual remedy. Git keeps a committed secret, so removing the line does not fix it.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0
metadata.aliases: [SECURITY-HARDCODED-SECRET-001], the shared core alias also carried by the agnostic node and its python-pytest realization
Stack-neutral obligation, and one of only two rules in this family that ports verbatim from the python-pytest sibling coder.security.hardcoded-secret. The five patterns are language-neutral.
Realized by bun_security_hygiene_detector (implementation type validator, ref bun_security_hygiene_detector)

additions.text: Credentials in covered files are read from process.env; previously committed secrets have been rotated.
additions.justification: Turns the source fix_hint and the rotation term into checkable compliance evidence. This adds no new obligation.

trace.note: Applies to every secret literal in covered files, whether new or existing
Disposition strict kept as written; no baseline policy is inferred
